key_insight: NavTrust exposes how embodied navigation agents (VLN and OGN) break down under realistic input corruptions by providing a unified, systematic benchmark to measure trustworthiness and robustness. It reveals gaps between nominal performance and real-world reliability.
problem_solved: Existing navigation evaluations measure nominal performance only, ignoring sensor/modal corruption and environmental noise that occur in deployment; NavTrust fills this gap by benchmarking robustness and trust for embodied navigation agents under systematic corruptions.
method: Design a unified corruption suite that injects controlled perturbations into inputs (e.g., visual, language, sensor noise) applicable to both Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) and Object-Goal Navigation (OGN).
Run standardized evaluation protocols across agents and tasks to quantify degradation in navigation success, safety, and reliability under each corruption type.
Provide aggregated trustworthiness metrics and analysis tools to compare models, identify failure modes, and guide robustness improvements.
impact: NavTrust gives researchers and practitioners a practical way to quantify and compare the real-world reliability of navigation agents, helping prioritize robustness fixes and improving safety for deployment in noisy environments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: clean input → corruption module (visual, language, sensor) → navigation agent → robustness metrics
Grid of example corruptions (clean vs. corrupted images/transcripts) for quick visual comparison
Bar/line charts showing performance drop (success rate / SPL) across corruption types and severities
Radar or heatmap of trustworthiness metrics (robustness, safety, consistency) per model
paper_title: NavTrust: Benchmarking Trustworthiness for Embodied Navigation
paper_authors: Huaide Jiang, Yash Chaudhary, Yuping Wang, Zehao Wang, Raghav Sharma
